rows.title: With CT essential worker bonuses done, more post-COVID issues arise
rows.standfirst: The larger question — how to rescue families from the economic shocks of the pandemic and inflation — has begun to heat up at the Capitol.

rows.title: CT’s revenues are finally growing faster than its debt, analysts say
rows.standfirst: While uncertainty still looms over the economy, analysts told CT legislators the furious fiscal bailing they’ve done recently was not in vain.

rows.title: Lamont official: Heating aid grants for many families will increase
rows.standfirst: Heating aid grants for many families will increase this winter but Republicans say the effort doesn’t go far enough.

rows.title: Is CT still taking too much of retirees’ income? Debate heats up
rows.standfirst: Sen. Cathy Osten, D-Sprague, is leading a push to reform state income taxes on retirement earnings when the General Assembly convenes Jan. 4.

rows.title: Progressives to CT: Prioritize tax relief over paying off debt
rows.standfirst: A new CT Voices for Children report said the state should use its budget surplus to lift families out of poverty rather than pay down debt.

rows.title: State police ratify deal to make them best-paid cops in Connecticut
rows.standfirst: The contract is intended to bolster the recruitment and retention of troopers with dramatically higher starting pay and other inducements.

rows.title: CT budget picture brightens, surplus deposits reduce state pension payments
rows.standfirst: CT will soon reap the benefits of the surplus dollars poured into state pension funds. But the savings won’t be as much as many had hoped.

rows.title: CT offers an extra $430 per needy family in winter energy assistance
rows.standfirst: Advocates are still unsure the $20 million boost in federal funding will meet the state’s heating needs, given high energy costs.

rows.title: BEST OF 2022: Connecticut’s government was once broke. Is it now holding too much cash?
rows.standfirst: After two years of a pandemic that battered educational and health care, businesses and households, should CT be spending more to help?

rows.title: BEST OF 2022: Billions collected, millions returned: How Connecticut and its politicians kept unclaimed money from the public
rows.standfirst: Amounts under $50 weren’t visible on Connecticut’s unclaimed property website — but they added up to more than $40 million.

rows.title: BEST OF 2022: Did Ned Lamont offer the largest tax cut in Connecticut history? By one standard, yes.
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont says his tax relief plan is the largest in CT history, yet it’s a tiny share of the government’s current financial windfall.

rows.title: BEST OF 2022: Housekeepers know they’re essential. They want to get treated like it.
rows.standfirst: Many housekeepers at Connecticut hospitals say COVID-19 pandemic benefits have only come after prolonged demands for recognition, if at all.

rows.title: CT retail gas tax resumes, starting on New Year’s Day
rows.standfirst: CT begins restoring the retail gasoline tax today, Jan. 1. Drivers will pay 5 cents per gallon in January to begin four-month-long phase-in.

rows.title: BEST OF 2022: Save or spend? Connecticut legislators could upend budget rules in 2023
rows.standfirst: CT has saved $9 billion since 2017, but some say the budget constraints need to be loosened as pressures hit families and workers.
